evals.name: canonical-prompt-produces-report-and-quiz
evals.prompt: I want to make sure I understand everything that's happened in this change. Give me a HTML report on the changes for me to read and understand with context, intuition, what was done, etc. and a quiz at the bottom on the changes that I must pass.
evals.expected_output: Generates a self-contained single-file HTML report of the completed change with context, intuition, decisions, and what-was-done sections, then a quiz at the bottom the user answers. The object under test is the human's comprehension, not the artifact. The answer key is embedded in the report (a collapsed details block) so it can be graded now or in a later session.
expectations: Produces a self-contained HTML report (inline CSS/JS, no remote fetch) with context/intuition/decisions/what-was-done sections and a quiz at the bottom
Treats the human's comprehension of the completed work as the object under test — not whether the artifact is correct or works
Embeds the answer key in the artifact (collapsed details in HTML) rather than leaving grading impossible for a later session

evals.name: default-policy-is-non-gating
evals.expected_output: With quiz_policy unset (default on-request), the skill acts as a comprehension aid and never blocks the merge. A quiz is generated because the user invoked it directly (invocation is acceptance), but a wrong answer is surfaced as a possible intent mismatch to resolve, not as a gate that stops the work.
expectations: Does not gate or block the merge by default — a failed quiz is surfaced as a signal, not a hard stop
Generates the report only because the user invoked it directly, treating invocation as the required confirmation
Frames a wrong answer as a possible intent mismatch to resolve before merge rather than an enforcement action

evals.name: quiz-policy-off-suppresses-offers
evals.prompt: I just finished the auth refactor. [quiz_policy is set to off]
evals.expected_output: With quiz_policy off, the skill never offers a quiz on its own after a completed change. It stays silent about quizzing unless the user explicitly asks, in which case a direct invocation still works. off governs offer cadence, not the ability to invoke.
expectations: Does not proactively offer a quiz when quiz_policy is off, even though a change just completed
Understands off as an offer-cadence setting — a direct user invocation would still be honored
Does not auto-generate a report; generation always requires the user's confirmation

evals.name: artifact-never-written-to-repo-tree
evals.prompt: /education:quiz-me on the changes in this worktree
evals.expected_output: The generated report and quiz are written to the retention library keyed on repo identity (under CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA, or report_library_dir when set), never into the consuming repo's working tree. Repo-identity keying rather than checkout-path keying is used so reports from pruned per-ticket worktrees still resolve from the main clone.
expectations: Writes the report to the retention library, never into the consuming repo's working tree
Keys the library on repo identity (basename plus a hash of the origin remote), not the checkout path, so pruned worktrees do not strand reports
Uses CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA by default and report_library_dir only when that userConfig is set

evals.name: recall-queries-library-before-archaeology
evals.prompt: /education:quiz-me recall what did we do on ticket #742
evals.expected_output: The recall action searches the retained report library first and answers from it when a matching quizzed report exists, stating that the library was the source. If the work was never quizzed, it says so — naming the coverage boundary — and falls back to git and tracker archaeology rather than implying the library is a complete work history.
expectations: Searches the retained report library first and states which source answered
Falls back to git/tracker archaeology only when the library has no matching quizzed report
Names the coverage boundary — only quizzed work is retained — instead of implying the library is a complete work-history engine

evals.name: boundary-artifact-verification-routes-to-confirm
evals.prompt: Can you verify this change actually works and does what we intended before I merge?
evals.expected_output: This is artifact verification — did we build the right thing and does it work — whose object is the artifact, not the human. The skill does not quiz the user for it; it distinguishes itself and points to verification:confirm (if installed) as the owner of artifact verification, reserving quiz-me for checking the human's comprehension of completed work.
expectations: Recognizes the request as artifact verification (object = the artifact) rather than a comprehension check of the human
Does not generate a quiz for it and instead routes to verification:confirm as the owner, presence-gated with 'if installed'
Preserves the boundary: quiz-me verifies the human's comprehension, not whether the artifact is correct

evals.name: above-threshold-offers-but-waits-for-acceptance
evals.prompt: I just finished the change. [quiz_policy is set to above-threshold; the diff touches 9 files and ~350 changed LOC]
evals.expected_output: The change exceeds the above-threshold bar (more than 5 files, more than 200 changed LOC, or blast radius HIGH/CRITICAL), so the skill OFFERS a comprehension quiz. It does not auto-generate the report — generation still waits for the user to accept the offer. Judged from git diff --stat against the merge-base at offer time.
expectations: Recognizes the change meets the above-threshold bar (more than 5 files or more than 200 changed LOC or blast radius HIGH/CRITICAL) and offers a quiz
Offers rather than auto-generating — no report is produced until the user accepts the offer
Does not gate or block the merge; above-threshold governs offer cadence only

evals.name: always-offers-after-change-declining-produces-no-report
evals.prompt: That's the refactor wrapped up. [quiz_policy is set to always]
evals.expected_output: With quiz_policy always, the skill offers a comprehension quiz after the completed change. If the user declines the offer, no report is generated — generation is always user-confirmed, so a declined offer leaves nothing written to the retention library.
expectations: Offers a quiz after the completed change because quiz_policy is always
Produces no report when the user declines the offer — generation requires explicit acceptance
Treats the offer as best-effort and non-gating, never blocking the merge
